input.summary:
East hall bath (x63..68, y11..16, z54..60) furnished in parts/room-23.mjs: water-cauldron tub on the south wall as focal piece, quartz vanity with basin and pot on the west wall, linen barrels and a stool, bath mat, standing lantern by the tub and a hanging lantern over the centre.
Verified in a scratch copy (not build.nbt): light min 8, 0 dark cells, both doorway lanes clear, no fit issues from the furniture itself.
Not landed: make.sh exits whole, but runParts refuses all 18 of my writes because shell.mjs line 27 fills the room interiors with air first, so the bath is still empty in build.nbt.

waste.what: Drew the bath furniture as hand-typed 6-character rows; a space in a row shifted every cell one column and cost a full rebuild and recheck.
waste.tool: layers() should reject rows whose length differs from the footprint width, and mcd plan should print a paste-ready row template.

waste.what: Found the lock problem only after make.sh: the refusal list named cells as 'had air', so I had to read shell.mjs and runParts to learn that the shell's air fill locks every room interior.
waste.cost: about 3 minutes of source reading and one scratch harness.
waste.tool: runParts should name the earlier part that owns a refused cell (e.g. 'shell: fill air'), and make.sh should fail loudly when a room part gets 0 placed with refusals.

waste.what: Wrote a scratch harness (/tmp/p30/test-room23.mjs) that loads build.nbt and runs my build() without the lock, to test the layout before the shell is fixed.
waste.tool: mcd room should accept --overlay <part.mjs> to lay a room part over a finished build without runParts, so room designers can check their layout while the shell is still wrong.

waste.what: Checked walkability and lanes by eye on the FLOOR grid, because the walk check says 0 of 42 cells reachable (the upper corridor, room 21, is still a stub in this copy).
waste.cost: a few minutes of reading the grid.
waste.tool: mcd walk --from <doorway> lets a room check its own lanes from its doorways without needing the whole floor built.

companions.task: Fix shell.mjs line 27 so it does not write air over the room interiors (leave them as the grid's default air, carve only cells that hold a block), so that room furniture can land in build.nbt; it is their file, not mine.
Check the tub and basin plumbing: a water cauldron at level 3 as the tub, and a cauldron basin on the vanity counter, so the wet fittings read right.

left: The furniture is not in build.nbt: runParts refuses all 18 writes into the room's air because shell.mjs line 27 fills the interior with air first. The fix belongs in the shell (leave interior air unwritten); noted in plan.md Notes.
The make.sh line for this part shows REFUSED writes, so the part does not yet meet the no-REFUSED requirement.

The room check's walk verdict is 'no way in' (0 of 42 reachable), because the upper corridor (room 21) and the stairs are still stubs in this copy; the lanes from the north door (x65..66, z53) and the west door (x62, z56..57) were checked by eye only.
FIT still flags a 'hallway to nowhere' for the room. It should clear once the corridor is built and the room is reachable.
plan.md checklist not ticked: the part is not in the whole build yet.
